title: Object Shape Stabilizer for Monomorphic Inline Caching
subtopicTitle: V8 Internals: Hidden Classes & Inline Caches
problemStatement: Implement `stabilizeObjectShape(obj, fieldOrder)` that produces a normalized object containing the specified fields in deterministic declaration order, ensuring all instances share the exact same V8 Hidden Class transition chain.
interviewTrap: Initializing { a: 1, b: 2 } vs { b: 2, a: 1 } creates two separate V8 Hidden Classes. When passed to a shared function, the call site becomes polymorphic, doubling lookup overhead.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: V8 assigns a Hidden Class (Map) to every object. Adding properties in different orders or using 'delete' splits the transition tree and degrades inline caches from Monomorphic (fastest) to Megamorphic (hash table lookup fallback).
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Hidden Class Transition Tree Alignment.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is a Hidden Class (Shape/Map) in V8 and why does property initialization order matter?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In V8, JavaScript objects do not store property keys in individual hash tables. Instead, V8 assigns each object an internal hidden class (called a `Map` or `Shape`). When properties are added, the object transitions to a new Shape. If two objects are created with properties added in different orders (`{a:1, b:2}` vs `{b:2, a:1}`), V8 creates TWO DIFFERENT hidden classes, forcing inline caches into a slow polymorphic or megamorphic state.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: High-signal performance engineering question regarding V8 JIT internals.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does the 'delete' operator deoptimize objects in V8?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `delete obj.prop` mutates the shape transition tree, forcing V8 to abandon fast property access and demote the object to 'Dictionary Mode' (slow hash table lookup), slowing down property access by 10x-50x.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of V8 property representation modes.

realWorldUseCases.description: Initializing particle vectors with consistent constructors to ensure monomorphic inline cache optimization in TurboFan.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: class Point { constructor(x, y) { this.x = x; this.y = y; } } // stable shape

howToExplain.opening: V8 optimizes object property access using Hidden Classes (Shapes). Objects initialized with identical property keys in identical order share the same shape, enabling blazing-fast Monomorphic Inline Caching.
keyPoints: Objects share shapes when properties are initialized in the exact same order.
Always initialize all properties in constructors, even with null values.
Avoid using delete; assign null or undefined instead to preserve object shape.
Stable shapes enable TurboFan JIT compiler to emit direct memory offset reads.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Writing shape-friendly code allows JavaScript to run at speeds approaching compiled C++.
analogies: A standard car assembly line: every car receives doors, then wheels, then paint. Changing the order for one car disrupts the whole robotic factory line.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding properties to objects dynamically outside constructors based on conditional logic.
commonMistakes.why: Creates branching shape transition trees that turn monomorphic inline caches polymorphic.
commonMistakes.correct: Always initialize all properties in the constructor (e.g. this.prop = null).

followUpDeepDive.question: What are In-Object Properties vs Descriptor Arrays in V8?
followUpDeepDive.answer: V8 reserves space for initial properties directly inside the object's contiguous heap allocation ('In-Object Properties'). Properties added later overflow into an external property array, requiring an extra pointer dereference.
